speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Digital technologies have transformed the way we work and live.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Today, technology companies are among the fastest growing in the world and occupy an increasing share of the Fortune 500 list.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Singapore must develop our tech ecosystem and ride this growth to create more opportunities for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Increasingly, companies are basing their investment decisions on the availability of talent instead of traditional factors, such as the cost and availability of land.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Unfortunately, there is a global shortage of tech talent, and competition is intense.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: France overhauled its French Tech Visa six months ago to make it easier for tech talent to work in France.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Closer to home, Thailand introduced a SMART visa programme this year to attract highly skilled tech professionals.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: If Singapore sits back and does nothing, we will almost certainly be left behind.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We have only a small window to build a critical mass of high-end professionals, startups and companies.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: There will only be a few such nodes globally.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: How we do today will decide whether we make it as a tech hub, or not.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: It is not only companies which are facing a shortage of tech talent.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Our Government is also using technology to transform our public services and serve businesses and citizens better.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The Government is, therefore, tapping on the same limited pool of local tech professionals as our companies.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We are accelerating our efforts to develop our tech talent while ensuring that Singaporeans remain at the core of our efforts.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The first prong of our talent strategy, ever since we achieved Independence, has been to develop our local workforce.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Our people are our most important resource and we spare no effort in nurturing them.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: In our efforts to widen our tech talent pool, we have been rapidly scaling up our local pipeline of tech professionals.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Our institutes of higher learning offer around 200 full-time tech-related courses today.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We are also investing significantly in building new capabilities, such as cybersecurity and artificial intelligence (AI).

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Together, these efforts will increase our baseline of tech skills and capabilities.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: As we develop our base, we must also stretch the top of our Singaporean crop.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We have connected Singapore to the world to secure frontier opportunities for Singaporeans through programmes, such as the Global Innovation Alliance (GIA).

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: GIA is a global network connecting Singapore to leading innovation ecosystems and key markets around the world.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Singaporeans and businesses will be able to gain overseas experience and connect and collaborate with their overseas counterparts through GIA.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: But even these efforts are insufficient because the demand for tech talent is far outstripping the local supply.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This is not just a Singapore issue; it is a global challenge.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The Straits Times recently reported that recruiting firm Michael Page said that the demand for technology jobs in Singapore rose by 20% in the last 12 months but there is a shortage of supply.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Companies have also given our agencies feedback that we lack experienced software engineers and product managers.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: They are looking for people who can take charge of the development and rollout of digital products at a global scale, instead of only working on specific components of the product.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: These are often people that can marry both technical leadership and commercial acumen, manage larger tech teams in the hundreds and thousands, and are highly valued because they are in short supply.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We need to complement our local pipeline with skilled workers from all around the world to meet the surging demand from companies that are already in Singapore and companies that we want to bring to Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The presence of workers from other countries and nationalities also provides opportunities for Singaporeans to work in globally competitive teams and advance the frontiers of innovation together.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: In a world where multi-sectoral, cross-discipline and cross-cultural teams are increasingly common, Singaporeans must learn how to work with people from all around the world.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This will increase their competitiveness as individual employees and make them more attractive to employers.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Alibaba, Grab, SAP and Taiger are examples of some companies which have plans to expand significantly in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Many of these companies have shared that the ability to complement their local workforce with global talent is essential for them to quickly scale their operations in accordance with their plans.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This is why we launched Tech@SG to help fast-growth tech companies, both local and foreign, to grow in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This programme is intended for companies with the commitment and ability to build teams and products in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: They will have to be incorporated in Singapore, have a digital or technology offering or have a business model built around proprietary technologies, research or hardware.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This will ensure the companies would have sufficient resources and readiness to internationalise and compete.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: In addition, Tech@SG will raise the quality of tech talent in Singapore and create more opportunities for our tech experts to team up with the best from around the world.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We must be prepared for these fast-growth companies to recruit the skills they most require.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: In the short term, these skills may come from global professionals.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: But we must take a strategic view on this to reap the long-term rewards for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We did so for the semi-conductor industry in the 1960s.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: At that time, many multinational companies (MNCs) in the industry came here and set up their core team which comprised mainly foreigners.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Over time, as these companies anchored themselves in Singapore, they began to rapidly grow their local pool of employees.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: They have also grown an entire generation of specialists and professionals in this area that enabled the semi-conductor industry of Singapore today.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Today, we have a similar opportunity to create a vibrant and dynamic tech sector, generating new and exciting job opportunities for yet another generation of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Visenze, an AI and image recognition company founded by four Singaporeans, now hires more than 60 tech professionals to form multinational teams that develop and improve their AI technology.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Abel Lim, a recent graduate from the National University of Singapore's School of Computing, learns about applying machine learning to real-life problems from colleagues in his team who come from around the world.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Together, their team makes improvements to Visenze’s algorithms.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Mastercard is an MNC currently spearheading the creation of new digital technologies in payment solutions and smart mobility in Singapore, powered by AI.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: These innovative activities require new capabilities that would need to be built up in the Singapore team.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: These equip them with new skills and allow them to work alongside senior experts from around the world.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Seliyan Silvarajoo is one such Singaporean who has undergone this programme.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: He started out as an intern at Mastercard and is now a senior digital product specialist.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Seliyan counts his experience learning from and working with a global and diverse team as critical to preparing him for his role in developing new and exciting products.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Besides companies like Mastercard and Visenze, we have a good stable of companies like the digital giants Google and Facebook that create good opportunities for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We need to be able to create an environment for Singaporeans to learn from the best and to thrive.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We need to grow our tech ecosystem and create exciting opportunities for all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: At the same time, this is a Government that has always sought to be honest with Singaporeans and has never shied away from explaining our challenges and sharing what needs to be done in order for us to grow and adjust to changing realities.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We will never stop putting Singaporeans at the heart of everything we do and will continue to develop every Singaporean to their fullest potential so that they can fulfil their aspirations and seize opportunities in Singapore and beyond.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: However, we must not go down the path of other countries which have started to put up barriers and take an inward-looking, protectionist approach, not just to trade, but including talent.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Doing so, we will only hurt Singapore whose success over the last 54 years has been built on our openness and courage to do what is necessary for our country.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: To this end, we will continue to do our best for each and every Singaporean while continuously building on our efforts to take Singapore into the next lap, with the world as our hinterland for trade and talent.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: I have three supplementary questions for the Minister.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: The second question: whether the agencies concerned in rolling out Tech@SG considered leveraging MOM's Capability Transfer Programme to roll out some of these knowledge transfer, skills transfer and capability transfer to Singaporeans?

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Thirdly, amidst this sense of uncertainty and quite dismal outlook in terms of the employment and job market, our focus is on helping, supporting and assisting fellow Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: I just wonder whether there are controls in place or will there be controls that will be instituted on Tech@SG to make sure that our local professionals, managers and executives are not compromised or prejudiced against?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The answer to the first question is a definite yes.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The second question: did we consider the Capability Transfer Programme?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Yes, that is one of the various instruments that we use to level up our own professional knowledge.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We will continue to do that and, where there are opportunities, we will even step up our gear to do that.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But having said that, as I have explained, even though we are churning out as many people as we can, as fast as we can, it is still not sufficient to meet the growing demand.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We must make sure that we do not miss the boat by losing the professionals, the startups and the companies for us to form a critical mass quickly.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: On the third point, it is precisely because of the uncertainties with the economic outlook that we have stepped up our gear to make sure that we build the next generation of companies in this sector.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: At this point in time, I would say that this forms part of our overall surgical measures to help our companies transform and expand their market presence.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We know that the current numbers are dragged down by the global electronics downturn, the wholesale and retail trade, and some of the precision engineering sectors.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: On the other hand, our economy is growing well in the financial services, ICT and many of the high-tech industries.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: This is why we must make sure that while we try to lift the bottom, we must never cap the top.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We must make sure that we can do all we can to help those companies that are growing the fastest at this point in time, suffering from the global shortage of tech talent, including many of our ICTs and AI companies, to make sure that the Tech@SG programme will give them the best chance possible to succeed and will not make them lose out to other companies from other countries who are competing for the global talent at this point in time.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
text: Now, we are doing Tech@SG for the tech sector.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
text: Will the Ministry of Trade and Industry consider or is it in the works to considering other sectors as well?

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
text: Because it is not just the ICT sector that needs foreign expertise or even data analytics, data science expertise.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
text: It could be the financial sector or many other professional services, and all these contribute quite significantly this year and, moving forward, to the economic growth of Singapore.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We are open to considering how we can work with the other sectors which are short of this talent at the global level.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We are not talking about S Pass holders, we are not even talking about the average Employment Pass holders.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We are talking about people who can manage programmers by the hundreds and thousands.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: These are the people who know and have the expertise to manage global teams of the hundreds and thousands of people, and these are in critical shortage.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: If China, France and Thailand are all doing this, we can understand how critically short we are at the global level.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, while everybody is trying to churn out as many as they possibly can within the time, everyone is also fighting for the available talent at this point in time.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: A few years ago, there was an initiative to increase the number of Singaporeans or work towards increasing the number of Singaporeans in leadership positions in the financial sector.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Is there a similar parallel initiative that the Government has in mind for Tech@SG?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I think the Minister raised some numbers about the number of students in our institutes of higher learning.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: But more upstream, in terms of taking on roles, since this is a long runway that we are looking at, does the Government have any plans in that regard?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: In fact, that is a very good example of how we do business.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We will continue to do this because we will never stay static and we will never say that we have done enough to get our locals into the top leadership positions.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: This is exactly the same spirit that we intend to do for all the new sectors.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: That is how, progressively, we are not shy to learn from the best in the world.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But as we learn from the best in the world, we want to make sure that our people have the best opportunities to learn from them, acquire those skills and maybe even go beyond.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: This must continue to be the Singapore way.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: This was how we built up the semi-conductor industry in the 1960s and 1970s and that will not change.
